title: Roasted Beetroot Soup
subtitle: Earthy roasted beetroot blended with orange and horseradish
excerpt: Beetroot roasted until concentrated and sweet, blended with stock and a squeeze of orange juice. A spoonful of horseradish cream sharpens each bowl. Vivid deep crimson, earthy, and satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beetroot soup appears in many European cuisines, from the Ukrainian and Russian borscht traditions to Scandinavian and British home cooking. The roasting method concentrates the beetroot's natural sweetness and gives the soup more complexity than boiling does. Orange juice cuts through the earthiness. Horseradish — fresh or from a jar — is a natural pairing and adds a peppery sharpness.

recipeTools.notes: Or a stand blender for a smoother result.

content.text: Wear gloves when peeling roasted beetroot: the juice stains permanently. Roast until a skewer slides in without resistance. The colour of the finished soup depends on how acidic the stock is: add a splash more orange juice if the colour looks dull.

items.preparation: freshly grated, or from a jar

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Wrap the whole beetroots loosely in foil. Toss the onion and garlic cloves with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and place in a small roasting dish covered with foil. Roast everything for 50 to 60 minutes until the beetroot is completely tender. Unwrap and cool for 10 minutes. Peel the beetroot with gloves on.
Roughly chop the beetroot and tip into a saucepan with the roasted onion and garlic. Pour in the hot stock and orange juice. Blend until completely smooth.
Reheat gently. Season with salt and pepper. Mix the horseradish into the crème fraîche.
Ladle into warmed bowls. Add a spoonful of horseradish crème fraîche to each bowl.
